newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia markets watchdog to reveal Astra buyers.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia markets watchdog to reveal Astra buyers.

text.p: Indonesia's capital market's watchdog plans to reveal who has been buying shares in Astra International as soon as Monday, the Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Saturday.

"Next Monday maybe we can announce the names of the investors who have been buying large volumes of Astra shares," the head of the Bapepam, the capital markets supervisory agency, I Putu Gede Ary Suta, was quoted as saying on Friday.
Shares of Astra, a diversified company which is Indonesia's largest carmaker, began rising at the beginning of last week on rumours that a takeover bid was in progress.
Brokers have said some 100 million shares, or about 10 percent of the company's equity, have since changed hands. The share closed at 3,775 rupiah on Friday, up from 2,625 on September 16.
Suta said every share transaction above five percent of a company's stock must be reported to capital market authorities within 10 days.
"But if it can be done in 48 hours why wait 10 days," he said.
Newspaper reports have said that three of President Suharto's children, all leading businesspeople, and a number of prominent tycoons are either buyers or prospective buyers of the company.
The reports have named Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardianti Rukmana and sons Bambang Trihatmodjo and Hutomo Mandala Putra as being linked to the buying.
They say plantations magnate Prajogo Pangestu, timber baron Mohamad (Bob) Hasan and tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna are also believed to be involved.

Mandala Putra is the sole beneficiary of Indonesia's controversial national car policy, which grants his joint venture with South Korea's Kia Motors tax and tariff breaks on the condition that local content requirements are met within three years.
Trihatmodjo, the head of the Bimantara group, has set up an automobile joint venture with Hyundai Motor Co, South Korea's largest car manufacturer.

While Sampoerna, head of cigarette maker Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, has confirmed he has been buying shares, he has not said how many. The other businesspeople have declined to comment on whether they are involved.
Astra's holdings are widely scattered and brokers have said a stake of around 20 percent would be enough to gain control.
But Astra is owned 8.26 percent by Toyota Motor Co and brokers have said it is unlikely that the Japanese firm will look kindly upon even indirect links with South Korean rivals.
